[{"name": "segment_popularity7", "idea": "Article's share of 7-day distinct buyers among customers whose dominant 90-day index group matches the user's, giving a segment-specific popularity (ladies, menswear, kids) that the global buyer counts cannot give to the mostly global candidate list.", "level": "pair", "sql": "WITH ig AS (SELECT t.customer_id, a.index_group_no, COUNT(*) AS n FROM tx t JOIN articles a ON t.article_id = a.article_id WHERE t.t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 90 DAY GROUP BY t.customer_id, a.index_group_no), dom AS (SELECT customer_id, index_group_no FROM (SELECT customer_id, index_group_no, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY n DESC, index_group_no) AS r FROM ig) z WHERE r = 1), sp AS (SELECT d.index_group_no, t.article_id, COUNT(DISTINCT t.customer_id) AS n FROM tx t JOIN dom d ON d.customer_id = t.customer_id WHERE t.t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 7 DAY GROUP BY d.index_group_no, t.article_id), st AS (SELECT index_group_no, SUM(n) AS s FROM sp GROUP BY index_group_no) SELECT c.customer_id, c.article_id, COALESCE(sp.n, 0) * 1000.0 / st.s AS ag_seg_pop7 FROM cand c JOIN dom d ON d.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN st ON st.index_group_no = d.index_group_no LEFT JOIN sp ON sp.index_group_no = d.index_group_no AND sp.article_id = c.article_id WHERE st.s > 0;"},
 {"name": "channel_match90", "idea": "One minus the absolute difference between the user's 90-day online share and the article's 90-day online share, so online-only shoppers are steered away from articles that sell mainly in stores and vice versa.", "level": "pair", "sql": "WITH uc AS (SELECT t.customer_id, AVG(CASE WHEN t.sales_channel_id = '2' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) AS o FROM tx t JOIN users u ON t.customer_id = u.customer_id WHERE t.t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 90 DAY GROUP BY t.customer_id), ic AS (SELECT article_id, AVG(CASE WHEN sales_channel_id = '2' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) AS o FROM tx WHERE t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 90 DAY GROUP BY article_id) SELECT c.customer_id, c.article_id, 1.0 - ABS(uc.o - ic.o) AS ag_channel_match90 FROM cand c JOIN uc ON uc.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN ic ON ic.article_id = c.article_id;"},
 {"name": "user_repeat_propensity365", "idea": "Share of the user's distinct 365-day articles that they bought on two or more distinct days, a repurchase trait that tells the model how much to trust ui_tx and user_recent_rank for this user.", "level": "customer", "sql": "WITH ua AS (SELECT t.customer_id, t.article_id, COUNT(DISTINCT t.t_dat) AS d FROM tx t JOIN users u ON t.customer_id = u.customer_id WHERE t.t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 365 DAY GROUP BY t.customer_id, t.article_id) SELECT customer_id, AVG(CASE WHEN d >= 2 THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) AS ag_u_repeat_share365 FROM ua GROUP BY customer_id;"},
 {"name": "type_seasonal_shift_ly", "idea": "Smoothed ratio of the product type's distinct buyers in the target-aligned week one year earlier to the week before it, a seasonal momentum prior showing which categories rise into the coming week (e.g. knitwear into autumn).", "level": "article", "sql": "WITH ty AS (SELECT a2.product_type_no, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN t.t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 364 DAY THEN t.customer_id END) AS n1, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN t.t_dat < DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 364 DAY THEN t.customer_id END) AS n0 FROM tx t JOIN articles a2 ON t.article_id = a2.article_id WHERE t.t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 371 DAY AND t.t_dat < DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 357 DAY GROUP BY a2.product_type_no) SELECT a.article_id, COALESCE((ty.n1 + 10.0) / (ty.n0 + 10.0), 1.0) AS ag_type_season_ly FROM articles a LEFT JOIN ty ON ty.product_type_no = a.product_type_no;"},
 {"name": "dept_decay_affinity90", "idea": "Exponentially time-decayed count (0.9 per day) of the user's 90-day rows in the candidate's department, a short-term shopping-intent signal that weights last week's category far above the flat 90-day department share.", "level": "pair", "sql": "WITH ut AS (SELECT t.customer_id, a.department_no, SUM(POWER(0.9, date_diff('day', t.t_dat, DATE '{A}') - 1)) AS w FROM tx t JOIN users u ON t.customer_id = u.customer_id JOIN articles a ON t.article_id = a.article_id WHERE t.t_dat >= DATE '{A}' - INTERVAL 90 DAY GROUP BY t.customer_id, a.department_no) SELECT c.customer_id, c.article_id, COALESCE(ut.w, 0.0) AS ag_dept_decay90 FROM cand c LEFT JOIN articles a ON a.article_id = c.article_id LEFT JOIN ut ON ut.customer_id = c.customer_id AND ut.department_no = a.department_no;"}]
